title: Indirect discourse in context
subtitle: Keep the reported claim distinct from the reporting act.
overview: Indirect discourse places a claim under a verb of saying, knowing, hearing, or thinking. The outer verb tells who reports; the inner clause gives what is reported.
Greek may use ὅτι/ὡς clauses, infinitive constructions, or participles. Read the construction selected by the text rather than converting all reports into one English pattern.

items.grc: λέγει αὐτοῖς ὅτι δεῖ τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου πολλὰ παθεῖν.
items.en: He says to them that the Son of Man must suffer many things.

items.grc: οἴδαμεν ὅτι ἐκ τοῦ θανάτου μεταβεβήκαμεν εἰς τὴν ζωήν.
items.en: We know that we have passed from death into life.
